Card Name: Uptake and Survival of African Swine Fever Virus in Mealworm and Black Soldier Fly Larvae
Veszély jellemzése: Pathogen Transmission: Insects raised on substrates containing animal waste may harbor pathogens that can be transmitted to animals and humans. This is particularly concerning with viruses like the African swine fever virus (ASFV).    Virus Survival: Studies have shown that ASFV can survive in larvae such as the mealybug and black soldier fly. This poses a risk of spreading the virus to susceptible animals through consumption of these insects.    Food Safety: If insects are used as food or feed, there is a potential risk to the food chain if they carry pathogens from contaminated substrates.    Regulatory Concerns: Current regulations limit the use of animal by-products in insect farming due to these risks, necessitating thorough risk assessments and safety evaluations before any changes can be made.

Veszély jellemzése: Bioaccumulation in Fish: Tralopyril and its degradation products can accumulate in the muscle tissue of salmon, raising concerns about residue levels in the fish consumed by humans. Card Name: Anti-cholesterol supplements, the European Commission intervenes: “Limit the dosages, they can give side effects”

Dosage Risks: Without regulation, consumers might inadvertently consume doses higher than recommended, increasing the risk of adverse effects. Interactions with Other Medications: Monacolin can interact with other drugs, potentially leading to harmful effects, which might not be monitored without medical oversight.    Quality and Consistency: Supplements can vary in monacolin content, leading to inconsistent dosing and effectiveness, unlike prescription medications which have strict quality controls.
